- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) in recent history, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling after peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model may lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day of lag.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early divergence (e.g., first 3–5 days deviate), reduce forecast slope to match sentiment trend.
